name: Clematis
lede: Clematis is a bluish violet named for the flower, recorded in color dictionaries from 1899 on.

sections.title: The flower's name
sections.body:
*Clematis* is defined by Paterson as a bright bluish violet, like the flower of the same name [1]. The same dictionary files it among the blues, not the purples, which shows how loosely a bluish violet sits between the two families [1].

The swatch here is from Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* (1930), where the name is first recorded in 1899, on plate 42 [2]. It is dark and saturated, with a lightness of 29 on the LCH scale [2]. Its closest named neighbor in our library is [[indigo]], at a CIEDE2000 distance of 4.2 [2].

The color books say nothing more about a dye, a pigment or a fashion tied to this name, so an honest account stops here.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Clematis is very rare as a painted color. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers at least 1% of the canvas in only one work [3]. It is rarer than 86% of the named colors in the archive [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
